absent: Numeric values of remap, sync, sealing, protection, mapping and fault constants.
Full layouts of address space, mapping area, remap descriptor, userfaultfd context and file structures.
Internals of helpers that perform the actual move, split accounting, population, notification, file sync and cache maintenance.
Lock ordering with other locks and behavior when killable acquisition is interrupted beyond returning intr.
Sealing modification, hugetlb alignment, area iteration and lookup helpers beyond their contracts used here.
No-MMU region allocation, mapping and unmapping engines beyond the entry wrappers shown.
Audit, reference counting, sysctl registration, slab allocation and iterator copy semantics beyond the calls observed.

findings.text: Remap completion for a userfaultfd context emits a remap notification carrying source, destination and length, then blocks until the monitor acknowledges; a missing context makes the operation a silent no-op.
Failure unwind for a remap with userfaultfd releases one changing reference and the context reference, warning if the counter would go negative; a missing context makes the operation a silent no-op.

A mapping is eligible for batched multi-area moves only when userfaultfd is not armed on it and either no special placement helper is present or the area belongs to a known-good family covering shared memory, hugetlb, or transparent huge page placement.
Shared-memory status holds when an area is anonymous shared memory or when its operation vector is the shared-memory vector.

Preparation for remap rejects a missing area, a sealed area, and a misaligned hugetlb area, then records size delta and operation kind and defaults the destination to the source when no new address is implied, returning early when no fresh mapping will be created.

Preparation forbids duplicating a private area with zero source length, forbids retain-source moves on non-expandable or pfn-mapped areas, and treats shrink as allowing boundary crossing by clamping the examined length, while requiring the source range to sit inside one area.

Preparation for a size change marks locked expansions for later population, rejects page-index wrap, rejects expansion of non-expandable or pfn-mapped areas, and checks future locking and virtual-memory expansion limits before permitting growth.

Parameter checking for remap allows only the documented flag subset, requires page alignment of the source, rejects empty destination length and oversized lengths beyond the task limit, and skips further checks when no new address is implied.

When a new address is implied, parameter checking requires the destination range to fit in the task limit and be page aligned, requires move permission for fixed placement, forbids resizing with retain-source, and forbids overlap between source and destination.

Move execution walks every area intersecting the source interval, fails on a leading gap, preserves gaps between consecutive areas at the destination, and advances the destination cursor after each successful piece.

Move execution allows multiple areas only when each area permits batching, otherwise it requires exactly one area covering the whole range, prepares and executes each piece in turn, returns the first piece result, and expects the write lock to stay held with no expansion population.

Top-level remap aligns both lengths, validates parameters, acquires the write lock in killable fashion, checks split limits, dispatches to batched move or single-area lookup plus prepare plus execute, then unlocks, populates locked growth, and finally reports to userfaultfd with success state.

Top-level remap holds the address-space write lock from admission checks through execution, releases it once before post-processing, and performs locked-region population and userfaultfd notification without the lock.

The remap system entry strips addressing tags from the source while leaving the destination tagged so range checks reject aliased destinations, initializes a remap descriptor with empty userfaultfd state and lists, and delegates to the common engine.
Seal preparation scans the requested interval and reports a gap when areas do not fully cover it, using the previous end to detect holes including a trailing hole.
Sealing walks covered portions and, for each not yet sealed portion, updates protection state through a modify helper and then marks the area sealed under write access.
Range sealing acquires the address-space write lock in killable fashion, fails when unmapped holes exist, otherwise seals, and always releases the lock before returning.
Sealing of the zero page runs only when the process personality permits that mapping, sealing exactly one low page and emitting a rate-limited warning on failure.

The seal system entry requires zero flags, removes addressing tags, requires page alignment, aligns length with overflow and wrap checks, treats empty ranges as success, and delegates to range sealing.

The sync system entry removes addressing tags, accepts only async, invalidate and sync options, requires page alignment, rejects combined async plus sync, rounds length to pages with overflow checks, and treats empty intervals as success.

Sync walks areas in order, skips holes while remembering deferred unmapped status except for pure async which exits early, rejects invalidate on locked areas, translates address ranges to file offsets, and for shared file-backed sync drops the lock around a ranged flush before resuming.
Sync holds the address-space read lock while scanning, releases it across each file flush and reacquires afterwards, and returns the flush error if any else the deferred unmapped status.
No-MMU builds keep a highest frame value, a heap-stack gap, a committed-pages counter, a region slab cache with an address-ordered tree root, and an empty file operation vector for generic mappings.
Object size inquiry returns zero for null or non-direct addresses, slab size for slab folios, containing area span for ordinary folios with a covering area, and folio size otherwise.

No-MMU virtual allocation is direct slab allocation with compound semantics and without high memory; node, range, alignment, protection and caller arguments are ignored, zeroing variants request cleared memory, and 32-bit variants collapse to the same paths.
User-visible virtual allocation marks the covering area with a user-map flag under the address-space write lock after successful allocation.
No-MMU translation from virtual address to page or frame number goes through the direct-map conversion without table lookup.
No-MMU vector read clamps the byte count to avoid address wrap and then copies the linear range into the iterator.
Scatter mapping, RAM mapping and RAM unmapping abort in no-MMU mode and report failure, while alias invalidation is a no-op.
Page insertion and page-array mapping helpers unconditionally reject their inputs in no-MMU mode.

The break system entry in no-MMU mode leaves the break unchanged when outside start and end limits or equal to current, shrinks by direct update, and grows by flushing instruction-cache coverage for the new span before updating.
No-MMU exposes a writable trim-pages control backed by an integer with zero minimum through a single sysctl table entry.
No-MMU memory initialization sets up the committed-memory counter, creates the region cache with panic and accounting semantics, registers the trim control, and initializes area state.
Exact area lookup succeeds only when a single area starts and ends exactly at the requested bounds, otherwise it reports absence.

No-MMU mapping entries audit the call, acquire a file reference for non-anonymous requests, delegate to the common pgoff mapper, and release the reference; the legacy entry copies a user structure and rejects unaligned offsets.
The legacy mapping argument container carries protections and flags alongside requested address, length, descriptor and file offset as address-sized words.
No-MMU unmapping acquires the address-space write lock, delegates to the common unmapper, releases the lock, and returns the inner status.
The unmap system entry in no-MMU mode forwards address and length to the locked unmapper.
Remap accepts distinct options for fixed destination, permitted move, and retained source.
Sync accepts distinct options for asynchronous writeback, invalidation, and synchronous writeback.
Sealing requires no option bits and page-granular aligned ranges.
Remap fails when source and destination overlap, when destination arithmetic would exceed the task limit, and when page-index arithmetic would wrap.
Generic file operations for no-MMU provide an empty operation vector.
No-MMU log output prefixes messages with the module name.
